name: Region Pairs
plain_english: Two Azure regions paired for disaster recovery, same geography, at least 300 miles apart.
african_examples: Nairobi and Mombasa are paired if Nairobi floods, Mombasa keeps running.
Same-country pairing means compliance stays inside one jurisdiction (Kenya).
common_wrong_answer: Regions in a pair are restored simultaneously during an outage.
correction: One region in the pair is prioritized for restoration; the other follows.

name: Availability Zones vs Sets
plain_english: Availability Zones are separate datacenters within an Azure region, each with independent power, cooling, and networking. Availability Sets are separate virtual machine racks within a single datacenter.
african_examples: Availability Zones are like 3 separate buildings in Nairobi's Industrial Area, each with its own backup generator. If one catches fire, the other two keep running.
Availability Sets are like putting your servers on different racks within the SAME building. When maintenance happens, only some go down.
common_wrong_answer: Availability sets cost extra on top of VM pricing.
correction: Availability sets are free you only pay for the VMs. Zones are preferred for new workloads where supported.

name: Storage Redundancy (LRS/ZRS/GRS/GZRS)
plain_english: Azure Storage keeps multiple copies of your data to protect against failures. LRS 3 copies in 1 datacenter. ZRS 3 copies, one in each of 3 zones.
african_examples: LRS 3 copies on the same shelf in one M-Pesa shop.
ZRS 3 copies, one in each of 3 M-Pesa shops across town.
GRS copies in Nairobi AND a backup in Dar es Salaam. GZRS 3 shops in Nairobi 1 in Dar.
common_wrong_answer: GRS lets me read from the secondary region any time.
correction: Not by default you need RA-GRS for read access to the secondary before failover.
